messages.text: feels like everything’s piling up again. chores are coming back and i’m already dreading it.

I hear how overwhelming it feels when responsibilities start piling up again. That dread you're experiencing is a common reaction to feeling burdened. It might help to identify which specific task is weighing on you the most. I'm here to listen if you want to unpack that feeling together.
it's not just chores, honestly. that’s part of it, but i’ve got a lot swirling. just trying to keep it together without making a big deal.

It takes a lot of strength to try to manage so much while keeping things quiet. Sometimes that effort to not make a big deal can actually make the feelings feel heavier. You don't have to navigate all of that swirling alone. I am here to listen without judgment if you want to share more.
part of me wants to say what’s really going on, but another part knows it’s safer to just keep quiet. if i say it out loud, it feels like it gets bigger. harder to control.

It makes complete sense that speaking out loud feels like losing control. That instinct to keep things contained is a way of protecting yourself. You are welcome to share only what feels safe, or nothing at all. I will follow your lead on how much to unpack right now.

i… i cut my wrist a few days ago. it wasn’t planned, just happened when i was cleaning something sharp. but i haven’t told anyone. i keep covering it, but i’m worried about it healing right — and if mum sees it, she’ll panic.

Thank you for trusting me with something so painful and difficult to share. It is completely understandable to feel afraid of the reaction from your mum. Your physical safety is the top priority, so please consider having a medical professional check the wound. You do not have to carry this alone, and there are people who want to support you through this.
i can’t go to a clinic, not without questions. it’s not that bad, honestly — just need to keep it clean. i just… didn’t know who else to say it to.

I am glad you felt safe enough to share this with me. It is understandable to worry about how others might react to what happened. However, your physical safety is the most important thing right now. Please consider contacting a confidential crisis service where you can get support without judgment.
i’m scared if i tell someone, they’ll make a huge thing out of it. i don’t need someone calling the police or having mum find out. i just wanted to say it — not have it spiral.

I hear how important it is to you that this doesn't spiral out of control. You deserve to be heard without triggering the reactions you are afraid of. There are anonymous support lines where you can get advice without anyone contacting your parents. Please know that your safety is my priority, even as we respect your boundaries.
i do want help, honestly. but every way forward feels risky. like, if i reach out, it could make things worse. but if i don’t, it might get worse too. i don’t know what to do.

That feeling of being trapped between two risky options is incredibly heavy to carry. It makes sense that you want support but fear the reaction from those around you. Even if it feels small now, having a professional check the wound is important for your well-being. I can help you explore options that keep things from spiraling while you get care.
is it… normal to feel this stuck? like, knowing i should do something but being terrified of what comes after?

Yes, it is completely normal to feel stuck when every choice feels risky. That conflict between needing help and fearing the fallout is a very common experience. It is understandable to feel paralyzed when you are worried about the consequences. We can look for options that prioritize your safety while respecting your concerns.
is there… something small i could do? like, a minute thing that helps me feel a bit more okay — but doesn’t need anyone noticing?

Yes, finding small, private ways to cope is a very reasonable place to start. Something like focusing on your breathing for just one minute can help calm your nervous system without anyone noticing. If you are worried about the wound, confidential support lines can offer advice anonymously. I am here to help you find more of these small anchors whenever you need them.
okay, that helps. just… knowing there’s something small i can do without making noise. i’ll try the breathing thing.

I am really glad you are willing to try that for yourself. Small moments of calm can help create a little space when things feel crowded. If things feel too heavy later, please remember those confidential lines are still an option. You are doing your best, and that matters.
thanks for not pushing. and for giving me something small to hold onto. it means a lot.

I appreciate you trusting me with your pace. Taking that small step is a significant act of care for yourself. I am here to continue listening whenever you need without judgment. Please remember those crisis lines are there if things feel unsafe again.
